ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an ideal operational amplifier circuit, with ∞ marked inside the amplifier. The input signal on the left is Ui. Ui is connected through R1 to the inverting input terminal “-” of the op-amp; the output terminal Uo is also connected back through the feedback resistor R4 to the same inverting input node. Ui is also connected through R2 to the non-inverting input terminal “+” of the op-amp; this non-inverting input node is then connected to ground through R3. Reasoning: It is known that R1=R2=R3=10 kΩ, R4=20 kΩ, Ui=1 V. Under negative feedback of an ideal op-amp, V-=V+, and the input current is approximately 0. The non-inverting terminal forms a voltage divider by R2 and R3, so V+ = Ui·R3/(R2+R3) = 1×10/(10+10) = 0.5 V, therefore V- = 0.5 V. Write KCL for the inverting input node: (V- - Ui)/R1 + (V- - Uo)/R4 = 0. Substitute the numerical values: (0.5-1)/10k + (0.5-Uo)/20k = 0. Multiplying both sides by 20k gives -1 + 0.5 - Uo = 0, that is Uo = -0.5 V.

method.method_draft: First describe the image topology: the + input is driven by a divider R2-R3 from Ui to ground, while the - input is connected to Ui through R1 and to Uo through feedback resistor R4. From the text take R1=R2=R3=10 kΩ, R4=20 kΩ, Ui=1 V. Compute the non-inverting input voltage by the divider: V+ = Ui·R3/(R2+R3) = 0.5 V, so V- = 0.5 V. Apply KCL at the inverting node, with no op-amp input current: (V- - Ui)/R1 + (V- - Uo)/R4 = 0. Substitute values and solve for Uo, obtaining -0.5 V.
